title: Minimize Maximum Component Cost
summary: Given an undirected connected graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and edges with weights, and an integer k, you can remove edges to create at most k connected components.
statement: Given an undirected connected graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and edges with weights, and an integer k, you can remove edges to create at most k connected components. The cost of a component is the highest edge weight within it. Find the lowest possible maximum cost among all components after edge removals.
constraints: The input graph is connected with up to 50,000 nodes and 100,000 weighted edges.
Remove edges so at most k components remain.
Minimize the largest retained edge weight; isolated components cost zero.
hints: For threshold w, edges no heavier than w determine the fewest components achievable at that cost.
Run Kruskal until the component count reaches k.
Union edges by increasing weight and return the weight of the union that makes components no more than k.
Kruskal maximizes connectivity under each threshold, so the first qualifying threshold is optimal.
editorial: Kruskal maximizes connectivity under each threshold, so the first qualifying threshold is optimal.
